items.title: MDE and XDR APIs retire; migrate to Graph security API
items.fingerprint: The legacy Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR APIs retire on 1 February 2027 in favour of the Graph security API.

items.title: Federated Token Validation Policy — stricter default enforcement
items.fingerprint: Entra now blocks federated sign-in by default when internalDomainFederation doesn't match the user's UPN domain (federated domains configured before Dec 2025); rollout updated 2026-08-18, review federation config or sign-ins fail with AADSTS5000820.

items.title: SSPR to require registered authentication methods only
items.fingerprint: From 2026-11-07, SSPR stops accepting unregistered directory-sourced contact info (mobile/business phone, alternate email) for identity verification; the registration-nudge campaign begins 2026-10-05 (~14%% of current SSPR verifications reportedly rely on unregistered data) — audit registration coverage and prep helpdesk fallback now.

items.title: SSPR registered-methods enforcement begins
items.fingerprint: Enforcement of the SSPR registered-methods requirement begins on 7 November 2026.

items.title: MDE support ends for Amazon Linux 2 on ARM64
items.fingerprint: Defender for Endpoint stops supporting Amazon Linux 2 on ARM64 on 31 October 2026.

items.title: System-preferred authentication applies to first-factor sign-in
items.fingerprint: System-preferred authentication extends to first-factor sign-in from 30 September 2026, changing which method users are offered first.

items.title: Passkeys by default; Microsoft-provided SMS and voice MFA retiring
items.fingerprint: Passkeys become the default registration path on 1 September 2026 as Microsoft-provided SMS and voice MFA begin retiring.

items.title: EWS retirement and EWSAllowedAppIDs enforcement
items.fingerprint: Exchange Web Services access is restricted to app IDs listed in EWSAllowedAppIDs from 30 September 2026.

items.title: memberOf operator in dynamic group rules stops working
items.fingerprint: The memberOf operator in dynamic-membership group rules stops functioning 2026-11-03 with no error — affected groups silently freeze in last-known membership; audit now for any group (especially privileged/role-assignable) using memberOf and migrate before the date.

items.title: Passkey/passwordless allowed as the very first MFA registration method
items.fingerprint: Users can now register a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, or Authenticator passwordless sign-in as their first authentication-method registration instead of being forced through SMS/voice first; Phase 1 targets mid-October 2026 (exact day not yet published).

items.title: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO count as standalone MFA
items.fingerprint: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO are now treated as standalone multifactor credentials rather than single-factor plus a second prompt.

items.title: Defender for Endpoint Android app update required
items.fingerprint: Android devices must move to the current Defender app build by 15 September 2026 or lose protection features.

items.title: Teams Shifts Connection cmdlets removed in module 7.9.0
items.fingerprint: Teams Shifts Connection cmdlets disappear in Teams PowerShell Module 7.9.0 and dependent scripts stop working after the upgrade.

items.title: TERRL quota changes for new, trial and education tenants
items.fingerprint: From mid-September 2026 Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit quotas vary by tenant age and licence type, with trial tenants cut to 500 external recipients a day.

items.title: EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles extends to .clipchamp files
items.fingerprint: From mid-September 2026 the SharePoint Online setting covers Clipchamp project files alongside MP4, widening label inheritance to a new file type.

items.title: 60-day reminder: Windows 11 24H2 and Windows 10 LTSB 2016 end of updates
items.fingerprint: Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 stop receiving monthly security updates on 13 October 2026.

items.title: 60-day reminder: Windows Server 2022 mainstream support ends
items.fingerprint: Windows Server 2022 moves to extended support on 13 October 2026, keeping security updates only through 14 October 2031.

items.title: Azure PST Import into Exchange Online mailboxes
items.fingerprint: Admins can import PST files from Azure Blob Storage into mailboxes via PowerShell with readiness validation and reporting, from late August 2026.

items.title: CsTeamsEventsPolicy splits attendance and engagement report controls
items.fingerprint: A new policy separates attendance and engagement report controls for Teams Events from Teams Meetings, with four options, from mid-October 2026.

items.title: Health issue for missing Windows events from a domain controller
items.fingerprint: Defender for Identity adds a sensor health issue raised when no Windows events are received from a domain controller.

items.title: Health alert for missing domain controller network traffic
items.fingerprint: A health alert fires when a sensor stops seeing domain controller network traffic, catching a silent identity-detection blind spot.

items.title: Auto-labeling per-policy coverage report
items.fingerprint: A per-policy coverage report after simulation shows labelled and pending files and issues, retained 30 days, with nothing to enable.

items.title: Copilot Chat in Edge moves to cr.m365copilotapp.svc.cloud.microsoft
items.fingerprint: The commercial Copilot Chat endpoint used by Microsoft Edge changes by late September 2026, so network rules keyed to the old endpoint stop applying.

items.title: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening enforcement (CVE-2026-56155)
items.fingerprint: Microsoft enforces tightened ACLs on the AD FS DKM container from 31 October 2026 to address CVE-2026-56155; over-permissive ACLs let a low-privileged reader forge tokens.

items.title: Cross-tenant agent management from the Microsoft 365 admin center
items.fingerprint: Partners and enterprise admins can view and manage AI agents across connected tenants through GDAP authorisation.

items.title: Tenants auto-enabled into Defender Unified RBAC
items.fingerprint: Microsoft is auto-enabling tenants into Defender Unified RBAC, which can silently change what existing analyst roles can see and do.

items.title: User-managed sync file exclusions and .db-wal default exclusion
items.fingerprint: Users can manage their own file-level sync exclusions by default unless admins restrict it, and .db-wal files are excluded from sync by default from 5 October 2026.

items.title: Custom CSS layout properties in company branding retiring
items.fingerprint: Custom CSS layout/positioning properties in company branding retire 26 October 2026 (Secure Future Initiative); audit and remove deprecated properties before the deadline if using custom CSS.

items.title: Security Update Alerts in the Edge management service
items.fingerprint: Admins can set severity thresholds to be alerted when an Edge update carries significant security fixes, including zero-day patches.

items.title: Production PCA 2011 expiry and next-generation code signing
items.fingerprint: The Production PCA 2011 certificate expires and Microsoft moves to next-generation code signing; pinned trust stores and allow-lists must be updated by 19 October 2026.

items.title: Windows Information Protection and Application Guard retire in Microsoft Edge
items.fingerprint: Windows Information Protection and Defender Application Guard are removed from Microsoft Edge on 30 September 2026.

items.title: Passkey support for B2B guest users
items.fingerprint: Guest users in a B2B tenant can register and sign in with passkeys, extending phishing-resistant authentication to external identities.

items.title: Usage reports migrating to new domains
items.fingerprint: Microsoft 365 usage reports move to new service domains by 17 September 2026, which will break allow-lists and proxy rules pinned to the old hosts.

items.title: Admin policy to block identified external meeting bots
items.fingerprint: A new admin policy can auto-block identified external meeting bots from mid-September 2026; it ships default off.

items.title: Auto-labeling throughput rises from 100,000 to 500,000 files per day
items.fingerprint: Daily auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive rises fivefold, in preview September 2026 and general October 2026.

items.title: Excel Exchange Power Query connector replaced
items.fingerprint: The current Excel Power Query Microsoft Exchange connector is replaced by new Exchange Mail and Calendar connectors by April 2027, requiring manual workbook migration.

items.title: Release Planner retires and roadmap content moves to AI at Work
items.fingerprint: Release Planner retires on 15 November 2026 and the twice-yearly release wave model is replaced by continuous roadmap disclosure.

items.title: Unified response actions across linked identity accounts
items.fingerprint: From mid-October 2026 disable-account and force-password-reset run as one workflow across linked accounts in multiple identity systems and SaaS apps.

items.title: Unified identity timeline on the Identity page
items.fingerprint: The Identity page Timeline tab consolidates identity activity and alerts from multiple Microsoft security sources between mid-September and mid-October 2026.

items.title: Self-service identity domain migration: myaccount.microsoft.com to myaccount.cloud.microsoft
items.fingerprint: Entra is moving self-service My Account experiences worldwide to the cloud.microsoft domain, effective late November 2026 (exact day not yet published); allow *.cloud.microsoft in network/firewall/proxy allow-lists now.

items.title: App Governance drops Cloud Application Administrator role support
items.fingerprint: Cloud Application Administrator stops granting App Governance access on 26 September 2026 once Unified RBAC is enabled; holders must be reassigned to Security Administrator or another supported role.

items.title: Teams and Google Calendar sync retirement
items.fingerprint: Calendar syncing between Teams and Google Workspace ends in October 2026; account-matching data should be saved before then.

items.title: File Quarantine DLP action for SharePoint and OneDrive
items.fingerprint: DLP policies for SharePoint and OneDrive gain a File Quarantine action, a containment step that can also quarantine business files if misconfigured.

items.title: Hard delete for OneDrive and SharePoint via secure priority cleanup
items.fingerprint: Secure priority cleanup workflows gain a hard-delete capability for OneDrive and SharePoint content, an irreversible destruction path with obvious anti-forensic potential.

items.title: Launch Data Security Investigations from endpoint DLP alerts
items.fingerprint: An endpoint DLP alert can now launch a Data Security Investigation that gathers the exfiltrated files matching a DLP query, shortening the path from alert to scoped content review.

items.title: Data Security Triage Agent summaries surfaced in Defender XDR
items.fingerprint: Triage Agent summaries and categorisations now appear inside DLP alerts in Defender XDR rather than only in the Purview portal.

items.title: Reasoning trace and confidence score for agent-triaged DLP alerts
items.fingerprint: The Data Security Triage Agent now publishes a reasoning trace and a confidence score alongside each DLP alert it triages.

items.title: Security Detection Report in the Teams admin center
items.fingerprint: A Security Detection Report in the Teams admin center gives a central view of messaging security detections with export, adding a Teams-side telemetry surface outside the Defender portal.

items.title: Improved visibility and control for file downloads in Teams
items.fingerprint: Admins gain visibility and control over file downloads inside Teams, relevant to insider-risk and exfiltration policy.

items.title: Cross-tenant message recall
items.fingerprint: Exchange Online gains the ability to recall messages already delivered to recipients in a different tenant, a cross-tenant action that can remove evidence after delivery.

items.title: DLP policy sync SLA cut from two hours to 30 minutes
items.fingerprint: Microsoft reduces the published DLP policy sync SLA from up to two hours to 30 minutes, so a policy change reaches enforcement four times faster.

items.title: Granular access policy controls for custom organizational data attributes
items.fingerprint: Admins gain finer control over who can read custom organizational-data attributes, including those feeding Copilot experiences.

items.title: DLP for Copilot external web search
items.fingerprint: DLP can stop sensitive information reaching external web search grounding in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.

items.title: People Skills removal and deletion admin control
items.fingerprint: A new admin control permanently removes the organization’s entire People Skills library from the tenant, giving a deletion path for inferred profile data.

items.title: Report a Security Concern in Teams meetings
items.fingerprint: Teams meetings gain a user-facing Report a Security Concern control, creating a new end-user reporting stream the SOC has to triage.

items.title: Permissions audit log improvements
items.fingerprint: Purview improves audit logging of permission changes, which matters for investigating privilege escalation.

items.title: Malicious URL protection for Teams chat and channels in Gov clouds
items.fingerprint: Teams malicious URL detection and warning is extended to GCC, GCC High and DoD.

items.title: App-centric management extended to GCC High and DoD
items.fingerprint: App-centric management for controlling third-party app access reaches GCC High and DoD tenants.

items.title: Retention policies for Microsoft 365 Copilot memory
items.fingerprint: Data Lifecycle Management retention now covers Copilot memory, closing a governance gap on a persistent agent data store.

items.title: Purview DLP for calendar events in Outlook mobile
items.fingerprint: Purview DLP policies extend to calendar events in Outlook for iOS and Android, closing a channel that previously carried sensitive content unchecked.

items.title: Purview DLP wait-on-send for Outlook mobile and Mac
items.fingerprint: Outlook for iOS, Android and Mac gain Purview DLP wait-on-send, so a message is held until DLP evaluation completes rather than leaving before the policy is applied.

items.title: Authenticator for Android uses Google Play Integrity for jailbreak detection and fails closed
items.fingerprint: Documentation now states Authenticator for Android uses the Google Play Integrity API for jailbreak detection and denies access when the API is unavailable unless the policy is disabled.

items.title: Activity logs legacy connector and storage integration API retire
items.fingerprint: The legacy Activity Logs connector and storage integration API retire on 15 September 2026; ingestion must move to diagnostic settings or Activity Log data stops arriving.

items.title: Computer Vision API v1.0 through v3.1 retire
items.fingerprint: Five Computer Vision API generations retire on the same day, so most legacy vision integrations break at once.

items.title: Custom block response code and body for Application Gateway WAF
items.fingerprint: WAF block responses become customisable, which changes the fingerprint that both attackers and block-rate detections see.

items.title: Azure Virtual Desktop (Classic) retires
items.fingerprint: Classic Azure Virtual Desktop deployments lose support on 30 September 2026, leaving remote-access infrastructure outside ARM RBAC and unpatched.

items.title: Connect to AKS clusters using Azure Bastion
items.fingerprint: Bastion gains a tunnelled administrative path to AKS API servers, a new privileged access route to baseline.

items.title: Shareable link expiration generally available
items.fingerprint: Azure Bastion shareable links can now be given an expiry; links created before this had none and were standing remote-access exposure.

items.title: Container Log V1 and Service Bus control-plane APIs retire
items.fingerprint: Container Log V1, the Get AlertSummary API and three Service Bus control-plane API versions all retire on 30 September 2026.

items.title: v2.0 API and v2.1 container retire
items.fingerprint: The v2.0 API and the self-hosted v2.1 container both retire on 31 August 2026, leaving unpatched container images in the estate.

items.title: IPv6 support in Azure Firewall
items.fingerprint: IPv6 traffic can now traverse Azure Firewall, so IPv4-only rules and log parsers silently miss it.

items.title: Azure Functions 1.x support ends
items.fingerprint: Version 1.x function apps keep running but stop receiving security updates after 14 September 2026.

items.title: Get AlertSummary and smart groups APIs retire
items.fingerprint: Alert-summary and smart-group retrieval stops on 30 September 2026, breaking triage tooling built on those endpoints.

items.title: Azure SRE Agent VNet integration
items.fingerprint: The SRE Agent now runs inside customer network controls, becoming a privileged in-network automation identity to scope and log.

items.title: Azure VPN Client for Linux retirement
items.fingerprint: The Azure VPN Client for Linux retires on 31 August 2026.

items.title: Conditional Access custom controls become read-only
items.fingerprint: Conditional Access custom controls become read-only on 30 September 2026; policies still referencing them must move to authentication strengths or external methods.

items.title: Entra Connect Health agent 4.5.2614.0
items.fingerprint: Entra Connect Health agent 4.5.2614.0 improves agent credential security and key-rotation support; Microsoft dates the release only to August 2026 and prints no day.

items.title: Cloud Sync can source sAMAccountName from onPremisesSamAccountName
items.fingerprint: Enhanced synchronization can source sAMAccountName for hybrid users from onPremisesSamAccountName, changing an attribute many SIEM correlation rules key on.

items.title: Request-on-behalf-of licensing requirements clarified
items.fingerprint: Examples were added clarifying which licences the requestor and the target user each need for request-on-behalf-of access package requests.

items.title: Entra Backup and Recovery covers Agent ID objects
items.fingerprint: Entra Backup and Recovery documentation now lists agent user accounts, agent identity blueprints, agent identities and agent identity blueprint principals among the recoverable object types.

items.title: Entra Connect 2.5.79.0 end of support
items.fingerprint: Version 2.5.79.0 itself leaves support on 23 October 2026, so the September upgrade should target a later build.

items.title: Entra Connect Sync — mandatory upgrade or ALL sync services stop
items.fingerprint: Standing notice: all Microsoft Entra Connect Sync services stop working on 2026-09-30 for any server not on version >= 2.5.79.0 (shipped May 2025) — a hard cutoff with total sync outage as the consequence, not a soft degradation; verify tenant-wide version now.

items.title: External ID customer-facing passkey credential management API
items.fingerprint: New preview API lets customer-facing apps let end users list, register, and delete their own passkeys via delegated permissions.

items.title: Global Secure Access macOS client v1.1.26060207
items.fingerprint: Adds Home Network traffic control, a Connections page, agentic (AI agent) traffic detection/security policy support, Secure DNS bypass, MSAL sign-in/stability fixes; optional upgrade.

items.title: Global Secure Access Windows client v2.32.294
items.fingerprint: New 'Prefer local network' option for subnet-overlap scenarios, faster tunnel creation, removes LastMile-for-Office-365 telemetry, bundles .NET Runtime 10.0.9; optional upgrade.

items.title: Identity Protection legacy risk policies retire
items.fingerprint: The legacy user-risk and sign-in-risk policies retire on 1 October 2026 and must be rebuilt as Conditional Access policies.

items.title: Identity Protection "attacker-added device" response scope clarified
items.fingerprint: Terminology changed from 'Device disablement' to 'Attacker-added device'; docs now explicitly enumerate the automated response: device object disabled, token issuance blocked, refresh tokens revoked, sessions revoked — informational for SOC runbooks.

items.title: Mover workflow templates gain automatic access-package assignment removal
items.fingerprint: Mover lifecycle-workflow templates now include a 'Remove all access package assignments' task with a 15-day default removal timer (customizable, including immediate); opt-in customization recommended.

items.title: Black Hat research: passkey assertion replay & malware abuse ("Pass-the-Passkey")
items.fingerprint: Disclosed and now-patched flaw let Windows event logs capture full passkey assertions, replayable for up to 10 minutes by anyone with log read access (incl. Global Admin impersonation); unpatched attack classes remain (MFA-fatigue passkey flooding, synced-passkey exfiltration, browser-hook passkey detour) — deploy PAWs and CA device-compliance requirements for admins.

items.title: Inbound provisioning can now explicitly clear target attribute values
items.fingerprint: New opt-in capability lets inbound provisioning explicitly clear target attributes when source values are null/empty, instead of leaving stale target values as before.

items.title: SCIM API reference clarifies mailNickname derivation and immutability
items.fingerprint: mailNickname may be omitted at creation and is derived from the characters before the first @ in userName; it cannot be removed later via PATCH.

items.title: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice MFA fully retire
items.fingerprint: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice MFA are fully retired on 1 February 2027.

items.title: Customer-managed telephony provider list publishes
items.fingerprint: Microsoft publishes the supported customer-managed telephony provider list and terms in the Microsoft Security Store 2026-09-18 — informs whether an org with a genuine regulatory need to keep SMS/Voice has a viable carrier path before the 2027-02-01 full cutover.

items.title: Customer-managed telecom provider information via Security Store
items.fingerprint: Customer-managed telecom provider information must be supplied through the Microsoft Security Store by 18 September 2026.

items.title: Entra Tenant Governance reaches general availability
items.fingerprint: Tenant Governance is GA, making Tenant Governance Administrator a live privileged role that belongs in access reviews.

items.title: Token Protection for Apple platforms (iOS/iPadOS/macOS) reaches GA
items.fingerprint: Token Protection (binds tokens to a device to mitigate token-theft/replay) for Apple platforms moved from preview to GA; extend Token Protection Conditional Access policies to Apple platforms now that it's GA.

items.title: EntraIdSignInEvents replaces AADSignInEventsBeta on 19 October 2026
items.fingerprint: The EntraIdSignInEvents table page states that on 19 October 2026 it replaces AADSignInEventsBeta; custom detections migrate automatically but API-run and externally saved queries do not.

items.title: Phased disablement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) begins
items.fingerprint: Exchange Online begins phased EWS disablement 2026-10-01 (full retirement 2027-04-01); any SIEM connector, mailbox export/ingestion tool, or legacy add-in still calling EWS can start failing as phases roll out — run EWS Usage Reports and prioritize Graph API migration now.

items.title: Entra2ADExchangeOnlineAttributeWriteback (LES Writeback) documented
items.fingerprint: A cloud-to-on-premises attribute writeback path distinct from Exchange hybrid writeback is now documented, with its supported attributes and mappings.

items.title: Skype for Business Server hybrid EWS allow-list deadline
items.fingerprint: Hybrid Skype for Business Server deployments must set EwsEnabled=$true and add the SfB Server + desktop client App IDs to the EWS allow-list by end of August 2026, ahead of the Oct 1 EWS auto-switch, or SfB Server EWS calls to Exchange Online break.

items.title: Codename MDASH: cancel scan in portal + Azure DevOps connector
items.fingerprint: Agentic code scans (Codename MDASH) can now be cancelled directly from the Defender portal scan-details page; a new Azure DevOps connector lets security teams onboard ADO repos and trigger remote on-demand scans, extending coverage beyond GitHub.

items.title: External ID passkey credential management API
items.fingerprint: A credential management API lets External ID tenants enumerate and revoke customer passkeys programmatically.

items.title: FIDO2 hardware vendor attestation list updated to FIDO Metadata Service version 275
items.fingerprint: Model entries, AAGUIDs and compatibility indicators were refreshed and several vendor entries removed, which changes what an AAGUID allowlist admits.

items.title: Flexible federated identity credentials require immutable GitHub repository claims
items.fingerprint: Guidance now requires a flexible FIC to match sub plus repository_id or repository_owner_id rather than mutable name-based claims.

items.title: Access review scoping enhancements reach GA
items.fingerprint: New accessReviewPrincipalScope/accessReviewResourceScope/accessReviewAccessPackageAssignmentPolicyScope resource types plus a new accessReviewError surface for review-instance failures — governance/PIM admins should review the new error surface to catch silently failed reviews.

items.title: appliedByUser on assignSensitivityLabel
items.fingerprint: An app-only caller of assignSensitivityLabel can now name the user on whose behalf a label is applied, so labelling attribution survives service-principal automation.

items.title: Beta responseAction resource types removed for custom detections
items.fingerprint: A set of /beta responseAction resource types tied to custom-detection automated actions (initiateInvestigationResponseAction, moveToJunkResponseAction, disableUserResponseAction, etc.) are removed 2026-10-01, replaced by automatedAction/automatedActionSet on the detectionAction resource; inventory and migrate any SOAR automation or custom detection rule using the old types before the date.

items.title: coopEnforcement property on authenticationBehaviors (preview)
items.fingerprint: A new coopEnforcement property on authenticationBehaviors lets a tenant test or suppress Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy enforcement for browser-based authentication flows.

items.title: Graph createAlert action on the alert resource (preview)
items.fingerprint: A beta createAlert action lets an app inject alerts into Defender XDR with chosen severity, entities and incident linkage, with no detection behind them.

items.title: Cross-tenant access policy gains Microsoft 365 capability management
items.fingerprint: Cross-tenant access policies can now manage Microsoft 365 cross-tenant capabilities through the m365CapabilityBase resource.

items.title: distributionList.members (beta) standalone methods removed
items.fingerprint: The members property on the beta distributionList resource changed to an expandable relationship ($expand=members); previously separate standalone list/get-members methods were removed — any beta integration reading distribution-list membership the old way breaks immediately.

items.title: Entra directory object recovery API reaches GA
items.fingerprint: New recovery resource type and methods let you programmatically recover critical Entra directory objects from automatic point-in-time snapshots (inspect, preview, run recovery jobs, monitor progress); review who can call these high-privilege APIs and add to IR runbooks.

items.title: Legacy Microsoft Graph security alerts API retires
items.fingerprint: The legacy Microsoft Graph /security/alerts endpoint stops returning data on 15 October 2026, moved back from 31 August 2026; callers must migrate to /security/alerts_v2 and swap SecurityEvents.* permissions for SecurityAlert.*.

items.title: Lifecycle Workflows provisioning and workflow subject APIs promoted to v1.0
items.fingerprint: Lifecycle Workflows workflowSubject, subjectProcessingResult and activateAndWait move from beta to v1.0.

items.title: Lifecycle Workflows provisioning/workflow-subject model promoted to v1.0
items.fingerprint: A broad set of Identity Governance resources (workflowSubject, subjectProcessingResult, activateAndWait, provisioningAttributeMapping) promoted from beta to v1.0; plan migration if any automation still pins the beta endpoint.

items.title: Cross-tenant M365 capability management reaches GA
items.fingerprint: New m365CapabilityBase resource / m365Capabilities relationship manages which M365 experiences (calendar sharing, MailTips, cross-tenant migration) are enabled between tenants via cross-tenant access policy — relevant to B2B/multi-tenant security posture.

items.title: Entra directory object recovery API generally available
items.fingerprint: A new recovery resource type allows programmatic restoration of critical Entra directory objects from point-in-time snapshots, including previewing and running recovery jobs.

items.title: Microsoft Graph Toolkit and Microsoft Graph CLI retire today
items.fingerprint: Both the Microsoft Graph Toolkit component library and the Microsoft Graph CLI reach retirement on 28 August 2026 and receive no further security fixes.

items.title: Global Secure Access is GCC only, not GCC High or DoD
items.fingerprint: The Global Secure Access known-limitations page now states plainly that the service is available in GCC but is not supported in GCC High, Department of Defense or other government clouds.

items.title: GSA macOS client 1.1.26060207 adds Home Network traffic control and agentic-traffic policy
items.fingerprint: GSA macOS client 1.1.26060207 adds Home Network traffic control, a Connections page and agentic detection support that lets security policy apply to AI-agent traffic.

items.title: Global Secure Access web filtering V2 and V1-to-V2 migration documented
items.fingerprint: Learn now documents GSA Web Filtering V2 and how to migrate V1 policies; unmigrated policies can under-enforce during transition.

items.title: GSA Windows client 2.32.294 adds a Prefer local network option and drops Office 365 LastMile telemetry
items.fingerprint: Global Secure Access Windows client 2.32.294 adds a Prefer local network option for local-subnet overlap, ships .NET Runtime 10.0.9 and is the minimum build for Windows on Arm to receive the automatic Windows Update upgrades that begin in November 2026.

items.title: Identity Protection 'Attacker-added device' remediation
items.fingerprint: Identity Protection surfaces devices an attacker registered during a compromise and offers a direct remediation path from the risk detail.

items.title: Screen timeout setting for corporate Android devices
items.fingerprint: The Android Enterprise settings catalog gains a screen timeout setting that must be at or below the time-to-lock-screen value.

items.title: Separate device and work profile passwords on Android Enterprise
items.fingerprint: A Block one lock for device and work profile setting forces a distinct work-profile lock on Android 9 and later corporate-owned personally-enabled devices.

items.title: Limit how long an Android work profile can stay switched off
items.fingerprint: A new setting caps the number of days a COPE work profile may remain switched off, with a three-day minimum and 0 to disable.

items.title: OS 27 beta declarative settings including Web Content Filter and Siri
items.fingerprint: The Apple settings catalog exposes new declarative device management areas for iOS, iPadOS and macOS 27 betas for pre-GA testing.

items.title: Remove all eSIMs during a device wipe
items.fingerprint: A settings-catalog policy can now strip every eSIM profile from a corporate-owned Android 15 or later device as part of a wipe, closing a residual-identity gap at decommission.

items.title: Per-wipe eSIM removal choice for a single corporate-owned Android device
items.fingerprint: The single-device Wipe action gains a per-wipe eSIM removal option; by default a wipe now preserves the eSIM.

items.title: Newly available protected apps for app protection policies
items.fingerprint: Notion, Superhuman Mail, Calven, Heijmans, Notability, Ben for Intune and SDP On Premises join the protected apps list.

items.title: Windows settings catalog adds smart-card RDS disconnect and IE Protected Mode
items.fingerprint: Service release 2608 adds Windows settings-catalog options including Disconnect a Remote Desktop Services session when no smart card is present and Turn on Protected Mode for Internet Explorer security zones.

items.title: Windows devices flagged noncompliant when prohibited local AI agents detected
items.fingerprint: New Windows compliance-policy capability flags devices noncompliant when admin-defined prohibited local AI agents (example given: "OpenClaw") are found, with Conditional Access taking effect while noncompliant — plan the prohibited-agent list ahead of rollout.

items.title: Device Control (ASR) policy extends to MDE-attach devices
items.fingerprint: Endpoint security Device Control (ASR) policy will also apply to devices managed only via Defender for Endpoint security settings management (not Intune-MDM-enrolled) — check current ASR policy assignments now to confirm only intended devices receive it once this ships.

items.title: Google Play Strong Integrity enforcement (Android 13+)
items.fingerprint: From 2026-10-31, Android 13+ devices without a security update in the trailing 12 months are downgraded from Strong Integrity to Device Integrity, which can trigger app-protection conditional-launch blocks and compliance noncompliance (loss of CA-gated access); audit app-protection Min patch version settings now.

items.title: Audit enforcement level for the Defender Antivirus template for Linux
items.fingerprint: The Defender Antivirus template for Linux gains an Audit enforcement level so threats are detected and alerted without automatic remediation.

items.title: Memory scan setting for Defender Antivirus on Linux
items.fingerprint: Intune exposes a memory scan setting for Defender Antivirus on Linux under security settings management.

items.title: OS-version assignment filter reaches General Availability
items.fingerprint: Published in Intune's "Week of August 25, 2026 (service release 2608)" batch — in-window but absent from this morning's 15:26 UTC baseline; OS-version-based assignment filters for compliance/configuration policy targeting move from preview to GA. Review filter-based policy scoping for OS-version drift before relying on it for compliance enforcement.

items.title: Policy Configuration Agent & Change Review Agent removed from admin center
items.fingerprint: The Security-Copilot-powered Policy Configuration Agent and Change Review Agent, which translate compliance benchmarks into Intune settings-catalog policies, are removed from the admin center 2026-08-31; finish in-flight work now, existing policies already created are unaffected.

items.title: Scoped permissions moving to GA, becomes default for ALL tenants
items.fingerprint: Intune's Scoped-permissions setting (prevents merging permissions across role assignments sharing a permission category but different scope tags) is moving to GA and will become the default for every tenant; run the Permissions Assessment Report now to preview impact before it ships.

items.title: Unattended Remote Help sessions for Windows devices
items.fingerprint: Intune service release 2608 lets helpdesk staff open an unattended Remote Help session to a Windows device and take full control with no user present, using their own credentials.

items.title: Windows 365 for Agents security baseline
items.fingerprint: A new Intune security baseline supplies device-scoped Windows 11, Edge and Defender for Endpoint settings for Windows 365 for Agents Cloud PCs.

items.title: Lifecycle Workflow execution condition offset raised to 365 days
items.fingerprint: Workflow execution conditions accept an offset up to 365 days, allowing long-horizon joiner and leaver automation.

items.title: Access-package removal task extended to mover templates with a 15-day default
items.fingerprint: The remove-all-access-package-assignments task now applies to mover templates and defaults to a scheduled 15-day removal rather than immediate removal.

items.title: Lifecycle Workflows Time-based attribute V2 trigger
items.fingerprint: A V2 time-based attribute trigger lets leaver and mover workflows fire from any date attribute, tightening the window between an HR event and deprovisioning.

items.title: Microsoft SSO for Linux broker 2.0.2 switches device trust from registration to Entra join
items.fingerprint: From broker 2.0.2 Microsoft SSO for Linux uses Entra join instead of device registration for device trust; stale broker state and certificates must be cleaned or device-trust evaluation breaks.

items.title: Unified RBAC enabled by default for new customers
items.fingerprint: Starting August 2026, Microsoft Defender unified RBAC is automatically enabled for new Defender for Cloud Apps customers (no manual workload activation); for new tenants, verify analyst role assignments reflect unified RBAC rather than legacy MCAS-native roles — existing tenants are unaffected unless they opt in.

items.title: Defender for Cloud Apps file policies retire
items.fingerprint: File policies in Defender for Cloud Apps retire on 6 January 2027 in favour of Purview DLP.

items.title: Unified RBAC enabled by default for new Defender for Cloud Apps customers
items.fingerprint: From August 2026 new Defender for Cloud Apps tenants get Defender unified RBAC automatically instead of legacy Cloud App Security roles.

items.title: Android 1.0.9212.0102 shows last scan time
items.fingerprint: The Android malware protection card now shows the most recent scan time, giving help desks a way to confirm scan recency.

items.title: iOS 1.1.80120102 adds Dynamic Preview Rings and retires in-app OS update prompts
items.fingerprint: iOS build 1.1.80120102 adds Dynamic Preview Rings and retires in-app OS update recommendations, so minimum-OS compliance must come from MAM or MDM policy.

items.title: Linux build 101.26062.0007 fixes mdatp health reporting offboarded devices as healthy
items.fingerprint: Fixes slow on-demand scans and an mdatp health bug that reported offboarded Linux devices as healthy, and enables engine signature verification by default.

items.title: Antivirus audit mode for Linux
items.fingerprint: MDE for Linux 101.26062.0007 and later can detect and alert on malware in real time without quarantining files or terminating processes.

items.title: Audit mode for Microsoft Defender Antivirus on Linux
items.fingerprint: New Audit enforcement level for Defender AV on Linux (Intune-managed and MDE-attach, requires MDE on Linux v101.26062.0007+) detects and alerts in real time without auto-remediation/quarantine; also shipped as an Intune endpoint-security-template option — confirm audit-mode hosts are clearly flagged so alert-only isn't mistaken for blocked.

items.title: Engine signature verification on by default on Linux
items.fingerprint: MDE for Linux verifies the antivirus engine signature before loading and refuses unverified engines by default; legacy verification settings are deprecated.

items.title: Offboard machine API supports Linux servers
items.fingerprint: The Offboard machine API now supports Linux, so decommissioning can remove sensor records at scale instead of leaving orphaned devices.

items.title: Offboarding API support for Linux (GA)
items.fingerprint: The Offboard machine API now supports automated offboarding of Linux servers (requires MDE on Linux v101.26062.0007+); optional automation opportunity for device lifecycle management.

items.title: macOS 101.26062.0011 surfaces MCP server configurations
items.fingerprint: macOS build 101.26062.0011 extends local AI agent discovery to Model Context Protocol server configurations on managed Macs.

items.title: macOS build 101.26062.0012 supersedes 101.26062.0011
items.fingerprint: Release notes list macOS 101.26062.0012 (release 20.126062.12.0, engine 1.1.26060.12000, signature 1.457.164.0) above 101.26062.0011; Microsoft dates both to August 2026 only.

items.title: Expanded automatic auditing for AD CS, AD FS, and Entra Connect servers
items.fingerprint: MDI sensor v3.x now automatically configures required Windows event auditing on AD FS, AD CS, and Entra Connect servers (including non-DC servers), improving telemetry completeness for certificate-services enumeration and Entra Connect account misuse detections without manual GPO/auditpol work.

items.title: Automatic auditing extended to AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect servers
items.fingerprint: Automatic Windows event auditing now configures AD FS, AD CS and Entra Connect servers running sensor v3.x, including non-domain-controller servers.

items.title: Vulnerability assessment for Microsoft Store applications
items.fingerprint: Store-packaged applications now appear in vulnerability assessment with a Software evidence view giving file path and a suggested hunting query.

items.title: Azure DevOps connector for agentic code scanning
items.fingerprint: Security teams can connect Azure DevOps organizations from the Defender portal and run on-demand agentic code scans on their repositories.

items.title: Codename MDASH scan cancellation reaches the Defender portal
items.fingerprint: Scan cancellation, previously available only in Defender CLI, is now also available from the scan details page in the Scans tab of the Microsoft Defender portal.

items.title: Office 2021 desktop apps and LTSC 2021 reach end of support
items.fingerprint: The Office 2021 perpetual suite and the Office LTSC 2021 family stop receiving security updates on 13 October 2026.

items.title: Auto-labeling simulation mode and policy Insights tab
items.fingerprint: Auto-labeling policies can run in simulation before enforcement and an Insights tab reports policy performance in both modes.

items.title: Auto-labeling policy "Insights" tab
items.fingerprint: New at-a-glance performance view (simulation vs. enforcement mode) in the auto-labeling policy details panel improves visibility into labeling policy health for DLP/IP governance auditing.

items.title: Entra Connect Sync minimum version 2.5.79.0
items.fingerprint: Entra Connect Sync servers below 2.5.79.0 stop synchronising after 30 September 2026.

items.title: Attacks on exposed AI gateways and control points
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Security Blog documents attacks against exposed AI infrastructure — LiteLLM gateway exploitation followed by cryptomining — and the control points that stop them.

items.title: MacSync Stealer behavioural pivot hunting guidance
items.fingerprint: Microsoft published hunting guidance for MacSync Stealer, which rotates domain infrastructure fast enough to defeat indicator-based blocking but keeps stable behaviour.

items.title: The patch window is collapsing
items.fingerprint: Microsoft argues the gap between disclosure and exploitation has closed far enough that compensating controls, not patch cadence, are what carry the risk.

items.title: Microsoft Sentinel in the Azure portal retires
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Sentinel is no longer supported in the Azure portal after 31 March 2027; the Defender portal becomes the only surface.

items.title: Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector API support ends
items.fingerprint: The Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector API stops being supported on 14 September 2026; custom log pipelines must move to the Logs Ingestion API.

items.title: SAP containerized data connector permanently disabled
items.fingerprint: The containerized SAP data connector agent is permanently disabled 2026-09-14 (announced Nov 2025, creation of new agents already blocked); analytics rules/workbooks/hunts/playbooks on SAP logs from it silently stop returning results — migrate to the GA agentless SAP connector before the date.

items.title: SAP agentless 1.1.12, BTP 3.1.1 and LogServ 3.0.5
items.fingerprint: SAP BTP 3.1.1 renames analytic rules with an SAP BTP prefix, which breaks automation referencing the old names, and LogServ 3.0.5 moves HANA detections to Syslog.

items.title: SAP Agentless/BTP/LogServ solution updates
items.fingerprint: SAP Agentless v1.1.12 (audit-log performance), SAP BTP v3.1.1 (new analytic rule for unaudited custom-app logins; existing rules renamed with an SAP BTP prefix — check saved references/automation by name), SAP LogServ v3.0.5 (ASIM content for RISE with SAP, HANA detections move to Syslog).

items.title: UEBA contextual anomaly insights on behaviour records
items.fingerprint: Anomaly context such as first-seen activity, unusual volume and threat-intel matches is attached directly to UEBA behaviour records.

items.title: UEBA behaviors layer adds Fortinet FortiGate coverage
items.fingerprint: UEBA behaviors now cover FortiGate firewall events from CommonSecurityLog, adding 40+ behaviors for admin activity (rapid reconfig, config backups, cert changes, security-service disruption) mapped to T1685, T1070, T1078, T1602.002.

items.title: 10 new UEBA anomaly-detection rules: Check Point, FortiGate, Zscaler, AWS GuardDuty
items.fingerprint: UEBA anomaly detection now ingests Check Point/FortiGate/Zscaler firewall-VPN-proxy events (CommonSecurityLog) and identity-linked AWS GuardDuty findings, adding 10 new anomaly rules (MITRE T1078, T1133, T1110, T1071, T1562, T1567, T1087.004); enable UEBA on the relevant connectors to benefit.

items.title: UEBA adds FortiGate behaviours and ten anomaly rules
items.fingerprint: UEBA adds over forty Fortinet FortiGate behaviours from CommonSecurityLog and ten anomaly rules covering Check Point, Fortinet and Zscaler VPN, firewall and proxy events plus AWS GuardDuty findings.

items.title: Optional claims reference labels synced passkeys as phishing-resistant MFA
items.fingerprint: Synced passkeys are now explicitly designated phishing-resistant MFA in the claims reference, and CBA designation is clarified as multifactor CBA.

items.title: Tenant creation requires a paid subscription
items.fingerprint: Creating a new Entra tenant now requires a paid subscription, removing the free shadow-tenant path users could take without procurement.

items.title: Token Protection GA on iOS, iPadOS and macOS
items.fingerprint: Conditional Access token protection is generally available on Apple platforms, binding refresh tokens to the device and blunting token-theft replay.

items.title: Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 ESU Year 3 ends
items.fingerprint: The third and final Extended Security Update year for Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 ends on 13 October 2026, after which no security updates exist at any price.

items.title: Windows Server 2016 end of support
items.fingerprint: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support on 12 January 2027.

items.title: What-if mode for Lifecycle Workflows
items.fingerprint: Reported capability to simulate a workflow's scope/impact before it runs, from Microsoft's August 2026 Entra monthly recap; primary page was client-rendered and only recoverable via search-engine snippet, so treat as lower-confidence until independently verified.

items.title: Defender AV template for Linux gains audit mode and memory-scan setting
items.fingerprint: Intune's Microsoft Defender Antivirus template for Linux adds an audit-mode option (matches MDE's own Aug 2026 Linux AV audit mode) and a memory-scan configuration setting.

items.title: New security baseline for Windows 365 for Agents Cloud PCs
items.fingerprint: Dedicated Windows 11/Edge/Defender for Endpoint baseline for agentic-workload Cloud PCs; deploy for any Windows 365 for Agents estate.

items.title: New Windows settings-catalog security options
items.fingerprint: Adds IE Protected Mode zone controls, an Edge 150 ADMX template, and a Disconnect RDP session if no smart card present hardening setting.

items.title: Windows Autopilot device association reaches GA
items.fingerprint: Binds a device to the organization pre-enrollment with hardware/TPM attestation, improving pre-enrollment device trust; admins should enable.

items.title: RBAC "scoped permissions" moving from Preview to GA as the tenant default
items.fingerprint: Scoped permissions become default behavior for all tenants on GA; run the Permissions Assessment Report first to avoid unintended access changes.

items.title: DLP policies extended to non-Microsoft connected apps
items.fingerprint: DLP policies now cover Box and Google Workspace via existing Defender for Cloud Apps connectors.

items.title: New Graph `recovery` resource reaches v1.0
items.fingerprint: Programmatic recovery of critical Entra directory objects from automatic point-in-time snapshots (inspect, scope, run recovery jobs, monitor); review IR/BCDR runbooks.

items.title: Access reviews gain explicit scope types
items.fingerprint: Access reviews gain explicit reviewer/principal/resource scope types (no query expression needed) plus error reporting on review instances.

items.title: New m365Capabilities resource for per-capability cross-tenant access
items.fingerprint: New m365CapabilityBase/m365Capabilities resources manage per-capability cross-tenant access (calendar sharing, MailTips, places booking, cross-tenant migration); review cross-tenant access policy if partner tenants exist.

items.title: `createAlert` action added for programmatic Defender alert creation
items.fingerprint: Beta createAlert action lets integrations programmatically create Microsoft 365 Defender alerts, including incident-linking and workspace routing.

items.title: Azure API for FHIR (Gen 1) retires
items.fingerprint: Azure API for FHIR (Gen 1) retires 30 September 2026; migrate healthcare workloads to Azure Health Data Services FHIR service.

items.title: Four legacy private network connector versions marked (Deprecated); urgent-update advisory added
items.fingerprint: Versions 1.5.612.0, 1.5.402.0, 1.5.132.0 and 1.5.36.0 of the Microsoft Entra private network connector (used by application proxy and Private Access) are now labelled (Deprecated); a new 'Earlier versions' advisory tells anyone on 1.5.612.0 or earlier to update immediately.

items.title: Universal Print: audit logging
items.fingerprint: Universal Print administrator and user activity (print job submissions, configuration changes, printer registrations) becomes available in Microsoft Purview's Unified Audit Log; revised by Microsoft on 28 Aug 2026 (v3), preview dated June CY2026, GA targeted January CY2027.

items.title: Universal Print: Logs and alerts (Azure Monitor integration)
items.fingerprint: Universal Print gains an Azure Monitor integration so diagnostic logs can be sent to a Log Analytics workspace for troubleshooting and custom alerting; revised by Microsoft on 28 Aug 2026 (v3), preview dated June CY2026, GA targeted January CY2027.

items.title: Insider Risk Management: preview content directly in alerts
items.fingerprint: Insider Risk Management alerts now let authorized reviewers preview referenced file content directly within the alert's activity explorer, without opening a case first; Microsoft revised this listing on 28 Aug 2026.

roles.name: B2C IEF Policy Administrator
roles.intro: Users in this role have the ability to create, read, update, and delete all custom policies in Azure AD B2C and therefore have full control over the Identity Experience Framework in the relevant Azure AD B2C organization. By editing policies, this user can establish direct federation with external identity providers, change the directory schema, change all user-facing content (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), change the requirements to complete an authentication, create new users, send user data to external systems including full migrations, and edit all user information including sensitive fields like passwords and phone numbers. Conversely, this role cannot change the encryption keys or edit the secrets used for federation in the organization.

roles.name: Global Administrator
roles.intro: This is a [privileged role](privileged-roles-permissions). Users with this role have access to all administrative features in Microsoft Entra ID, as well as services that use Microsoft Entra identities like the Microsoft Defender portal, the Microsoft Purview portal, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Skype for Business Online. Global Administrators can view Directory Activity logs. Furthermore, Global Administrators can [elevate their access](/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) to manage all Azure subscriptions and management groups. This allows Global Administrators to get full access to all Azure resources using the respective Microsoft Entra tenant. The person who signs up for the Microsoft Entra organization becomes a Global Administrator. There can be more than one Global Administrator at your company. Global Administrators can reset the password for any user and all other administrators. A Global Administrator cannot remove their own Global Administrator assignment. This is to prevent a situation where an organization has zero Global Administrators.

roles.description: This is a [privileged role](privileged-roles-permissions). Users with this role have access to all administrative features in Microsoft Entra ID, as well as services that use Microsoft Entra identities like the Microsoft Defender portal, the Microsoft Purview portal, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Skype for Business Online. Global Administrators can view Directory Activity logs. Furthermore, Global Administrators can [elevate their access](/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin) to manage all Azure subscriptions and management groups. This allows Global Administrators to get full access to all Azure resources using the respective Microsoft Entra tenant. The person who signs up for the Microsoft Entra organization becomes a Global Administrator. There can be more than one Global Administrator at your company. Global Administrators can reset the password for any user and all other administrators. A Global Administrator cannot remove their own Global Administrator assignment. This is to prevent a situation where an organization has zero Global Administrators.

roles.name: Global Reader
roles.intro: This is a [privileged role](privileged-roles-permissions). Users in this role can read settings and administrative information across Microsoft 365 services but can't take management actions. Global Reader is the read-only counterpart to Global Administrator. Assign Global Reader instead of Global Administrator for planning, audits, or investigations. Use Global Reader in combination with other limited admin roles like Exchange Administrator to make it easier to get work done without the assigning the Global Administrator role. Global Reader works with Microsoft 365 admin center, Exchange admin center, SharePoint admin center, Teams admin center, Microsoft Defender portal, Microsoft Purview portal, Azure portal, and Device Management admin center.

graph.resource: Windows Azure Service Management API / Azure Resource Manager (App ID 797f4846-ba00-4fd7-ba43-dac1f8f63013)
graph.consent: Not admin-consent-required by default; a user can consent to this scope for an app unless user consent is restricted by tenant policy

displayText.Delegated: Access Azure Service Management as organization users (preserves existing Access Control)

descriptionByType.Delegated: Allows the app to access the Azure Resource Manager / Azure Service Management control plane (subscriptions, resource groups, and ARM resource providers) on behalf of the signed-in user, scoped to whatever Azure RBAC roles that user already holds.

graph.originNote: Baseline inventory of the Azure Service Management surface (queue position #1, due 31 Aug 2026 — inventoried 2 days early on this pass). Microsoft did not change this permission today; this catalog simply had not read this surface before. Unlike Microsoft Graph, Azure Service Management exposes no application-permission app roles of its own — app-only (service principal) access to ARM is governed entirely by Azure RBAC role assignments (Owner/Contributor/Reader/custom roles), not by a consentable application permission, so this surface's application-permission column is intentionally empty.
graph.impact: A user who consents to this delegated scope for a malicious or compromised app hands it Azure Resource Manager control-plane access scoped to every Azure role that user already holds — invisible in a Microsoft Graph permission audit, and (unlike most Graph permissions) not gated by admin consent by default in many tenants.
graph.action: Hunt Entra sign-in / OAuth consent logs for grants of resource app 797f4846-ba00-4fd7-ba43-dac1f8f63013 (Windows Azure Service Management API); review Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions > User consent settings to confirm whether user consent for this resource is restricted; treat any newly-consented app holding this scope as equivalent in blast radius to the consenting user's Azure RBAC role assignments.

history.note: Catalog baseline: Azure Service Management surface inventoried (queue position #1), single delegated scope user_impersonation, GUIDs parsed from Microsoft's own New-EntraApplication PowerShell reference example.

graph: Microsoft publishes no severity or privilege tier for Graph permissions — any such rating shown elsewhere is a third-party tracker's own derivation, not Microsoft's.
Microsoft publishes no permission-to-directory-role mapping on the permissions-reference page.
Documented on each API method's own page, not on the permissions-reference page — not duplicated here.
roles: Microsoft publishes no mapping from a directory role's directory actions to equivalent Graph API permissions.
Microsoft publishes no attack-path/abuse narrative per role; any such narrative on a third-party site is that site's own analysis.
Microsoft's permissions-reference page does not state eligible-vs-active PIM assignment support per role in a structured field.
A tenant's live Microsoft Graph roleDefinition object can carry more actions than this documented page, because documentation lags the service — see actionsProvenance on each role entry.

roles.note: All 137 built-in Entra directory roles Microsoft currently documents on this page (135 from the 'All roles' summary table plus 2 roles nested only under 'Roles not shown in the portal': Microsoft 365 Support Engineer, Modern Commerce Administrator). Cross-verified against Microsoft's own GitHub source (137 [!INCLUDE] directives, 1:1 match). Azure RBAC built-in roles are NOT yet inventoried by this catalog — two Azure RBAC change records were captured this run (tracked-only, inInventory:false) but the full ~120-role Azure RBAC inventory is future work, not started. Updated 2026-08-29: added 3 built-in Entra directory roles visible in the roleDefinitions API but undocumented on Microsoft's role permissions-reference page (Entra SOC Identity Responder, Entra Customer Lockbox Approver, On Premises Directory Sync Account) per CLAUDE.md section 5e; docStatus backfilled across all 137 Entra directory role entries (2 Azure RBAC role entries in this catalog were left unchecked -- they need the Azure built-in-roles page, not the Entra one).

graph.note: All 951 'All permissions' entries plus all 58 Resource-Specific Consent (RSC) entries Microsoft currently publishes on the Graph permissions-reference page (951 + 58 = 1,009), parsed deterministically, every GUID taken verbatim from Microsoft's own printed identifiers. Plus 3 Office 365 Management APIs permissions, 11 Exchange Online app permissions, and 1 Azure Service Management delegated permission (user_impersonation) — queue positions #1-3 as of the previous run, now all three inventoried (Office 365 Mgmt APIs and Exchange Online on 2026-08-27/28, Azure Service Management on 2026-08-29). 10 further non-Graph API surfaces remain queued (see apis array). Updated 2026-08-28 -> 2026-08-29: added 13 live-but-undocumented UserAuthenticationMethod/UserAuthMethod-*.Delete.All permissions (found via Microsoft's global deployment map + a second tenant's SP export), plus docStatus backfilled across all 951 Microsoft Graph-surface permission entries (938 documented, 25 undocumented total: 12 already catalogued + 13 new).

apis.name: Microsoft Graph
apis.description: The primary Microsoft 365 / Entra API surface.
apis.socNote: The axis most SOC permission audits already cover — but not the only one.

apis.name: Office 365 Management APIs
apis.description: Audit-log / activity-feed / service-health surface used by SIEM ingestion.
apis.socNote: The SOC's core audit-log ingestion surface — a grant here (e.g. ActivityFeed.Read) is invisible in a Graph-only permission report.

apis.name: Exchange Online
apis.description: Exchange Online app-only/delegated permission scopes (e.g. full_access_as_app).
apis.socNote: full_access_as_app = whole-tenant mailbox read/write, separate from Graph Mail.ReadWrite.All — a common blind spot. Inventoried 2026-08-28: 11 permissions found across scattered EWS/IMAP/POP/SMTP/Admin-API OAuth docs — no single Microsoft reference page exists for this surface, so this list is not asserted complete the way the Graph/O365 Mgmt inventories are.

apis.name: Azure Service Management
apis.description: user_impersonation and Azure control-plane permission scopes.
apis.socNote: user_impersonation reaches the Azure control plane tenant-wide — rarely reviewed alongside Graph consent.

apis.name: SharePoint
apis.description: SharePoint Online / ACS app-only permission scopes.
apis.socNote: Legacy ACS app-only grants sit outside Graph consent reporting entirely.

apis.name: Microsoft Intune
apis.description: Intune Graph-adjacent and legacy API permission scopes.
apis.socNote: Device-management permission surface, partially overlapping Graph DeviceManagement.* permissions.

apis.name: Power BI
apis.description: Power BI REST API permission scopes.
apis.socNote: Report/dataset export scopes can expose sensitive dashboards outside Purview DLP visibility.

apis.name: Dynamics CRM
apis.socNote: CRM/Dataverse app-only grants are a common overlooked data-exfiltration surface.

apis.name: Azure DevOps
apis.description: Azure DevOps REST API / PAT scopes.
apis.socNote: Source-code and pipeline-secret access; a supply-chain-relevant surface.

apis.name: Microsoft Purview
apis.socNote: Overlaps with Graph eDiscovery/Security & Compliance scopes but has its own legacy surface.

apis.name: Power Automate
apis.description: Power Automate / Power Platform connector permission scopes.
apis.socNote: Connector-level consent for flows is a known low-code data-exfiltration path.

apis.name: Azure Storage
apis.socNote: SAS-token scopes bypass Entra sign-in entirely once issued — a blind spot for identity-centric monitoring.

apis.name: Azure RMS (Azure Information Protection)
apis.description: Azure Rights Management service permission scopes.
apis.socNote: Governs who can super-user decrypt protected content tenant-wide.

apis.name: Azure Data Explorer
apis.description: Azure Data Explorer (Kusto) cluster/database permission scopes.
apis.socNote: Relevant where Sentinel/hunting data lands in customer-managed ADX clusters.

comparedWith.method: Implemented CLAUDE.md's new section 5/5a-5e undocumented-permission methodology for the first time this run. Cloned microsoftgraph/microsoft-graph-devx-content fresh (permissions/new/provisioningInfo.json, D=1,885 names) and computed git log -S dates for the 13 UserAuthenticationMethod/UserAuthMethod-*.Delete.All permissions (all entered 2026-07-17). Fetched merill/microsoft-info's GraphAppRoles.csv and GraphDelegateRoles.csv in full (curl, not a summarizing fetch) for a second-tenant cross-check and the real GUIDs (never typed by hand). Fetched microsoft-graph-docs-contrib's permissions-reference.md in full (939 headings + 58 RSC rows) and diffed its name set against this catalog's Microsoft Graph-surface inventory: found 13 live, undocumented permissions (12 already catalogued, 1 new family of 13 delete-scoped permissions) and backfilled docStatus across all 951 Graph-surface permission entries. Fetched MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs's role permissions-reference.md in full and full-text-searched (not heading-only) for all 139 previously-catalogued role names plus the three roles CLAUDE.md names as undocumented; confirmed those three are absent from the raw source entirely and added them. No live tenant Graph service-principal read was available this run (no remote-desktop/Lokka connector attached) -- the 'A' (this tenant) side of the D/A/B/C comparison is this catalog's carried-forward inventory, not a fresh same-day SP read; this is stated in deploymentMap.limitation. Also repaired two real markup defects found in the inherited page: the masthead used legacy .inner/.meta/hand-authored classes instead of the CLAUDE.md section-1 masthead contract (.top-inner/.title-row/.hdr-tools/.counts/empty nav.anchors, plus the sixth undocumented-permissions count pill), and eight sections carried wrong canonical ids (changes/execsummary/newwindow/authwatch/products/hunting/socactions/today instead of delta/exec/new/auth/deep/kql/actions/top5), which had silently broken the Overview delta chart and several header-pill and chart-bar links -- both fixed this run by direct id/markup surgery, with all existing section content otherwise preserved untouched. Did lighter-weight freshness checks (not a full 40-source re-walk) on mc.merill.net, Entra fundamentals whats-new, Graph whats-new-overview, Sentinel/Defender XDR/Defender for Endpoint whats-new given three earlier passes already ran today (07:24 morning report, 13:50 and 21:11 diffs); found and verified 3 genuinely new/revised Message Center items (RM396782, RM519573, RM557189) not previously tracked.
